related_questions.question: What is the current protocol for a positive COVID test?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, the current recommendation is to isolate for at least five days from the start of symptoms or from the day of the positive test if asymptomatic, and to wear a mask for a total of 10 days. You can end isolation earlier if symptoms are gone or improving, and you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medication. Inform your close contacts and take precautions.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate for at least five days from the start of symptoms or from the day of the positive test if asymptomatic, and to wear a mask for a total of 10 days

list.snippet: Isolate: Stay home and away from others to prevent further spread.
Seek medical care: Consult with a healthcare provider for appropriate treatment.
Masking: Wear a high-quality mask (like an N95 or KN95) when around others for 10 days, even after isolation ends.
Monitor symptoms: If symptoms worsen, seek medical attention.
Inform contacts: Notify close contacts of your positive test result so they can take appropriate precautions.
End isolation: You can end isolation after at least five days if symptoms are gone or improving and you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medication.

text_blocks.snippet: The current treatment guidelines for COVID-19 are based on recommendations from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

list.title: Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir):
list.snippet: Recommended for adults and children (12 years and older) who are at high risk of developing severe illness. It should be taken within 5 days of symptom onset.

list.title: Molnupiravir (Lagevrio):
list.snippet: Recommended for adults who are at high risk of developing severe illness and are unable to take Paxlovid. It should be taken within 5 days of symptom onset.

Monoclonal antibody therapy is available for individuals who have tested positive for COVID-19 and are at high risk of developing severe illness. It should be administered within 5 days of symptom onset.
Supportive care: This includes rest, hydration, over-the-counter pain relievers, and fever reducers.
Oxygen therapy: May be required for individuals with severe illness.
Intravenous antibiotics: May be necessary for individuals with pneumonia or other bacterial infections.
Hospitalization is recommended for individuals with severe illness, such as those with difficulty breathing, low blood oxygen levels, or other medical complications.
Vaccination and boosters are the best way to prevent severe illness from COVID-19.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: These guidelines are subject to change as new information becomes available. It is important to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized treatment recommendations.
